a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences a feeding aversion and can be quite picky about what she eats, leading to difficulty in eating and potential nutritional deficiencies.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, squint, and hearing loss, particularly due to glue ear.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: She often rubs her eyes, especially when she's trying to focus on something. It's almost like she's straining to see clearly. We've noticed this happening more frequently during screen time or when reading.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Loud noises seem to overwhelm her easily. She gets frustrated in crowded or noisy environments, like shopping malls or playgrounds. Even at home, if there's too much background noise, she can become irritable.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her front teeth are noticeably larger than those of her peers. This has been a concern for us since it affects her smile and bite. We've been advised to monitor this closely and ensure good oral hygiene practices.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's an issue with one of her heart valves. Regular check-ups with the cardiologist have become a routine part of our lives now. So far, though, this hasn't limited her physical activities or energy levels significantly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Coordination seems to be a challenge for her. When running or engaging in sports, she appears less steady on her feet compared to her friends. It's subtle, but noticeable in certain situations.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Constipation has been an ongoing issue. She has trouble passing stools regularly and often complains of feeling bloated or uncomfortable after meals. Dietary adjustments have helped somewhat, but it remains a persistent concern.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Developmentally, she seems to lag behind her peers. Certain skills and milestones have taken longer to achieve than expected. This has prompted discussions about possible interventions or support systems to help bridge these gaps.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences slower weight gain compared to other kids her age, requiring nutrient-rich foods and supplements to support her growth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, with around 15% having heart conditions.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than average and some palatal abnormalities that the doctors keep an eye on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away, and she requires glasses to help correct this.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son experiences frequent episodes of heart-related issues, including valve abnormalities and potential congenital heart defects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, ranging from valve abnormalities to holes in the heart chambers and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has experienced difficulty with feeding since infancy, requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son frequently falls more than other children his age, potentially indicating a loss of balance or distance judgment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome fall more than other children their age.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Our son turns the volume of the TV up very high, even when we remind him it's already loud enough.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has experienced difficulty with vision, specifically with astigmatism and short-sightedness (hypermetropia).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Our son complains about tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods like ice cream or cold drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: Our son requires additional help in school, going to a mainstream primary school but needing more support in secondary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: Our son frequently falls more than other children his age, potentially indicating a loss of balance or distance judgment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome fall more than other children their age.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening for heart conditions: Regular check-ups with a cardiologist.
b) Monitoring for sensorineural hearing loss: Regular hearing checks starting at age 5.
c) Orthopedic evaluation: Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis.
d) Neurological assessment: Consider a neurological evaluation, especially if there are concerns about balance or distance judgment.

a) How this affects the patient: The child has hypermetropia, which means his eyes are crossed. It's been noticeable since he was little. We're worried it might affect his vision or cause discomfort.

a) How this affects the patient: The child has hypermetropia, which means his eyes are crossed.

a) How this affects the patient: The child has large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia of upper central incisors).

a) How this affects the patient: The child is experiencing delays in reaching certain developmental milestones and struggling to express himself clearly.

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: She sits very close to the TV or when reading books. This has been going on for a while now, and we're worried it might affect her eyesight.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There's fluid in her ear, which the doctor said could be causing some discomfort and possibly affecting her hearing.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing harder foods like meat or crunchy vegetables is difficult for her. We've had to adjust her diet accordingly to make mealtime easier.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: She was born with a septal defect, and we go for regular check-ups to monitor its impact on her health.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, she experiences epileptic seizures. We work closely with her neurologist to manage them effectively.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: She has a feeding aversion, especially to certain textures or tastes. It's been challenging to find foods she likes and will eat without fuss.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Her posture is noticebly different when standing or walking. We're not sure if it's related to another condition or just her overall development.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences a septal defect, requiring regular check-ups to monitor its impact on her health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, especially to certain textures or tastes, making it challenging to find foods she likes and will eat without fuss.

## 10) EDUCATION

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, of varying types.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, of varying types.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.
